definition: Quack.com was an early voice portal company.
details: The domain name later was used for Quack, an iPad search application from AOL.

explainer.lead: Quack.com was an early voice portal company, among the first to build services around spoken interaction rather than screens. That makes it a historical marker for voice as an interface to online content.

tiers.eli5: Imagine calling a phone number and talking to a computer to get news or information instead of typing a web address — that was the kind of service Quack.com built.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers studying voice interfaces treat it as an early data point on speech-driven portals; the lesson is that a voice product's brand and domain can outlive the original service and be repurposed.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is a company name, not a technical construct, and carries no formulas or stated limits.

explainer.example: The quack.com domain later hosted Quack, an iPad search application from AOL — a different product from the original voice portal company.
